 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:21290  CRL.RP No. 910 of 2014 Govindaiah vs State By Mandya on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66569399/
1  ORDER 1.

This Criminal Revision Petition is filed by the petitioner, being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 04.09.2012 in C.C.No.113/2008 on the file of the Court of J.M.F.C., Mandya and its confirmation judgment and order dated 05.09.2014 in Crl.A.No.108/2012 on the file of the Court of the II Additional Sessions Judge, Mandya, has filed this revision petition seeking to set aside the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below, wherein the petitioner /
accused is convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A and 506 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
2. The petitioner is the accused before the Trial Court and appellant before the Appellate Court.

Brief facts of the case are as under:
3. It is the case of the prosecution that, the petitioner and the complainant are husband and wife.
Their marriage was solemnized 17 years ago at Belur village, Mandya district.
It is alleged that, from the date of inception of the said marriage, NC: 2023:KHC:21290 the petitioner was not taking proper care of the complainant.
It is further alleged that, she was being harassed not only mentally but also physically by the petitioner.
Being frustrated by the act of the petitioner, and unable to tolerate the cruelty which she has meted out, she has decided to end her life and jumped into the well.
However, she was rescued.
It is alleged that, on 13.12.2007, the petitioner had demanded the complainant to hand over Rs.50,000/- by selling the property which was standing in the name of her mother.
Further, the petitioner threatened her that, if she did not fulfill his demand, she was threatened that, the petitioner would kill the children by pouring kerosene.
It is also further submitted that, on 31.01.2007 at about 11.00 a.m., the petitioner stated to have threatened the children by showing axe etc.,
The complaint came to be lodged by the complainant on 14.02.2007.
The jurisdictional police have registered a case in Crime No.55/2007 for the offences punishable under Section 498-A and 506 of the Indian Penal code (for short 'IPC').
After conducting investigation, they have submitted the charge sheet against the petitioner.
To prove the case of the prosecution, the prosecution examined, in all, 6 witnesses namely PWs.1 to 6 and got marked three documents Exhibit P1 to Ex.P3.
On the other hand, the accused has not led any evidence nor marked any documents on his behalf.
5. The Trial Court after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record, convicted the petitioner for the offence stated supra.
Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Appellate Court, the Appellate Court confirmed the judgment of conviction rendered by the Trial Court.
Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner has preferred this revision petition seeking to set aside the concurrent findings.

Govindaiah vs State By Mandya on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66569399/
2
6. Heard Ms. Bindushree L, learned Amicus Curiae appearing on behalf of the petitioner and Shri Rahul Rai, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.

7. Ms. Bindushree L, learned Amicus Curiae appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that,
ingredients of the NC: 2023:KHC:21290 provision of Section 498-A of IPC, would not attract as the averments of the complaint do not disclose the same.

It is further contended that, the Trial Court and the Appellate Court arrived at a conclusion that the petitioner is found guilty of the offence under Section 498-A and 506 of IPC is against the principles of law and also evidence, hence, it is liable to be set aside.

8. It is further submitted that, the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 who are the wife and daughter of the petitioner, their evidence ought not to have been considered by the Trial Court since they are interested witnesses.
The independent witnesses, even though stated to have supported the case of the prosecution, they are not eyewitnesses to the incident.
Their evidence ought not to have been considered by the Trial Court while analyzing the evidence.

9. It is further submitted that, even though PW.1 stated in her evidence that, due to the cruelty and harassment of the petitioner, she has attempted to commit suicide by jumping into the well and she was rescued by the villagers.
NC: 2023:KHC:21290
However, the prosecution has not chosen to cite the said persons as a charge sheet witnesses.

10. It is further submitted that, the evidence of PWs.1, 3 and 4 appears to be consistent with respect to the offence under Section 506 of IPC wherein the petitioner by holding axe, threatened PWs.1 and 2 on 31.1.2007 at about 11.00 a.m., PW.2 being the daughter has not stated anything about the incidents and also about the axe which the petitioner had allegedly shown to her and her mother.
Since PW.2 has not stated about the threatening by the petitioner by holding axe, the evidence of other witnesses in respect of the petitioner had holding the axe and threatened the PWs.1 and 2
is doubtful and the benefit should have been gone to the petitioner.
The Courts below committed an error in passing the order of conviction against the petitioner which requires to be set aside.

Making such submission, learned Amicus Curiae highlighted certain errors stated to have committed by the Courts below while appreciating the evidence and prays to set aside the concurrent findings recorded for conviction by both the Courts below.

Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader (for short 'HCGP') justified the concurrent findings recorded for conviction and submitted that, the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 inspires the confidence of the Court and there are no occasions to discredit the trustworthiness of the evidence of PWs.1 and 2. PW.3 who is an independent witness stated to be the eyewitness to the incident and supported the case of the prosecution.
Such being the case, it would not be appropriate to interfere with the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below.
Having submitted thus, learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

Govindaiah vs State By Mandya on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66569399/
3 12.

Having heard the rival contentions urged by the learned counsels for the respective parties and also perused the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below, it is appropriate to refer the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 for ascertaining any error or perversity committed by the Courts below in recording the conviction.

13. On perusal of the evidence of PWs.1 and 2, it appears that, in the examination-in-chief, PWs.1 and 2 are consistent in their evidence with regard to strained relationship NC: 2023:KHC:21290 existed between the petitioner and themselves.
It is also noticed in their evidence that, PW.1 being the wife has stated that, she and her children were suffering at the hands of the petitioner.

However,
the complainant, who is examined as PW.1, had not chosen to lodge the complaint against the petitioner in respect of the alleged cruelty and harassment at the earliest.

14. Now, it is relevant to refer the provision under Section 498-A of IPC, which read thus:
498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.--Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.--For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.] NC: 2023:KHC:21290
On careful reading of the above said provision, it appears that, the wilful conduct which is of such nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide.
15. The Courts below failed to appreciate the evidence of PW.1 properly.

Even though this Court is having no jurisdiction to appreciate the evidence, however, if there is an error committed by the Courts below in appreciating the evidence, interference by the Revisional Court is justified.
Admittedly, PW.1 is the wife and PW.2 is the daughter who deposed about the cruelty and harassment.
The evidence of PW.1 discloses that, she had tried to commit suicide by jumping into the well due to the cruelty, she was rescued by the persons who are the residents of her native village.
However, the persons who have rescued her have not been arrayed as witnesses to the case.
Hence, credence cannot be given to the evidence of PW.1 in respect of cruelty.

16. PW.2 being the daughter of the petitioner, though she has stated that there was a quarrel between PW.1 and the petitioner for petty reasons, she has not stated about the alleged attempt to commit suicide by PW.1.

PW.2 consistent in Govindaiah vs State By Mandya on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66569399/
4 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21290 her evidence that the petitioner was demanding PW.1 for Rs.50,000/-.

It is needless to say that, the couple have completed almost 20 years of their marital life as on the date of alleged incident, mere demanding money cannot be construed as demand of dowry unless it is specifically stated in that regard.
17. The Courts below failed to appreciate the defence of the petitioner.
There are several litigations pending between the petitioner and PW.1.
It is stated in the defence that, PW.1 had filed suit for partition and it was decreed.
As per the decree, 9 guntas of land came to the share of PW.1 and it was being sold to one Mr. Nanjundaiah and there was a sale agreement entered into between PW.1 and Nanjundaiah.
18. The Courts below failed to appreciate the evidence of independent witnesses namely, PW.5 and PW.4 who were stated to be the witnesses to the panchayath.
Both of them have stated that, there was a quarrel between PW.1 and the petitioner on 31.1.2007 at about 11.00 a.m. and both the witnesses have interfered and pacified the matter.
It is needless to say that, all the quarrels that had taken place for petty reasons cannot be construed as cruelty and harassment in the matrimonial cases.
The Courts below while appreciating the evidence of wife and other witnesses must be cautious and diligent as they are interested witnesses.

20. In the present case, the contradiction between PW.1 and PW.2 in respect of cruelty and harassment and delay in lodging the complaint and also the pendency of civil litigations between PW.1 and the petitioner assumes significant role.
The Courts below committed error in not considering these aspects and recorded the conviction which requires to be set aside.

21. In the light of observation made above, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER (i) The Criminal Revision Petition is allowed.

(ii) The judgment of conviction and order of  sentence, dated 04.09.2012 passed in  C.C.No.113/2008 by the Court of J.M.F.C.,
 Mandya and judgment and order dated Govindaiah vs State By Mandya on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66569399/
5  - 12 -  NC: 2023:KHC:21290 05.09.2014 passed in Crl.A. No.108/2012 by the Court of II Additional Sessions Judge at Mandya are set aside.
